guide.summary: GitLab documents user-delegated OAuth 2.0 with authorization code (PKCE) flows. The read_api scope grants read-only API access, which suffices for listing project issues, though it covers all groups and projects the user can access.

findings.title: User OAuth via registered application and authorization code flow
findings.detail: The authorization code flow (with or without PKCE) requires a registered application, giving an Application ID and Client Secret. PKCE is recommended for client and server apps. The user approves the requested scopes at /oauth/authorize, then the app exchanges the code at /oauth/token. Access tokens expire after 7200 seconds and can be renewed with a refresh_token.
findings.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts connect via OAuth

findings.appliesWhen: Before any OAuth authorization can be tested

findings.title: read_api grants read-only API access
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. GraphQL docs call it sufficient for queries, and api is required for mutations. It does not permit writes, which fits the never-create/update/delete rule. The user's own project access still limits visible issues.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing issue titles in a project the connected person can access

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Scope Access read_api Grants read access to the API. Sufficient for queries.

findings.title: Connected person must already have access to the project
findings.detail: The access token acts on behalf of a user. The Issues API lists issues for a project. Pagination uses page and per_page (default 20, max 100), Link headers, and keyset pagination for project issues, which is recommended for consecutive pages.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading issues from a specific project

steps.title: Register a user-owned OAuth application with redirect URI and read_api scope
steps.detail: In GitLab: avatar > Edit profile > Access > Applications > Add new application. Enter Name and Redirect URI, select scope read_api only, and save. Choose a confidential client (uses Client Secret) for this first test path. Record the Application ID and Secret. This prepares setup only; nothing has been registered yet.
steps.doneWhen: Application ID, Secret and an exact Redirect URI exist for the app.

evidence.quote: Enter a Name and Redirect URI .
The OAuth 2 Client ID in the Application ID field.
Select OAuth 2 Scopes as defined in Authorized Applications .

fields: APP_ID: Application ID from the saved application
APP_SECRET: Secret from the saved application
REDIRECT_URI: exact URI entered in the application

steps.title: Send test customer to GitLab consent page and check callback state
steps.detail: Generate an unpredictable STATE. Open this URL as the test user, who approves read_api: https://gitlab.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=APP_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE&scope=read_api (use <INSTANCE_BASE_URL> for self-managed). After approval GitLab redirects to REDIRECT_URI?code=...&state=STATE. Verify state equals what you sent. Not executed by this plan.
steps.doneWhen: Callback arrives with a code and a matching state value.

evidence.quote: Request authorization code. To do that, you should redirect the user to the

https://gitlab.example.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=APP_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE&scope=REQUESTED_SCOPES&root_namespace_id=ROOT_NAMESPACE_ID This page asks the user to approve the request from the app to access
The redirect includes the authorization code , for example:

fields: STATE: random value you generate and compare on callback

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: After consent, post the returned code to the token endpoint. Send client_id and client_secret as parameters (not also in a Basic header). Response contains access_token, refresh_token, expires_in 7200.
steps.doneWhen: Response returns access_token, token_type bearer and refresh_token.

You can send client_id and client_secret as request parameters, as shown, or in an
Example response: json {

fields: RETURNED_CODE: code query param from the callback

steps.title: List issue titles for a representative project (first page)
steps.detail: GET the project issues with the OAuth bearer token. Use a test project ID the connected user can access. Add scope=all so the default created-by-me filter does not hide issues, and per_page=100 with keyset pagination. Use --include to see the Link header. Expected: 200 with JSON array; titles at $[].title. Boundary check: inspect the token via /oauth/token/info and confirm scope is only read_api, and that this request log contains only GET calls. Never send write requests. First page of the collection with headers shown. Read the rel="next" URL in the Link header. Expected: array of issues, titles at $[].title. Boundary check: read-only GET only; confirm outgoing log has no non-GET calls.
steps.doneWhen: 200 response with an array of issues; each element has title; a Link header with rel="next" appears if more pages exist. 200 response; Link header with rel="next" present or absent (absent means single page).

evidence.quote: List all project issues
This endpoint supports both offset-based and keyset-based pagination. You should use keyset-based
--url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects?pagination=keyset&per_page=50&order_by=id&sort=asc" The response header includes a link to the next page. For example:
... Link: <https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects?pagination=keyset&per_page=50&order_by=id&sort=asc&id_after=42>; rel="next"

fields: PROJECT_ID: ID of a test project the user can access

steps.title: Boundary check: inspect granted scope
steps.detail: Call token info to confirm only read_api was granted. Do not attempt any issue write; read_api is documented as read access, but verify the grant and your outgoing request log rather than testing a prohibited write.

evidence.quote: /oauth/token/info . You must supply the access token, either:
--url "https://gitlab.example.com/oauth/token/info" The following is an example response:
read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.

steps.title: Keyset pagination: follow next link until none remains
steps.detail: Request the exact URL from the previous response's Link header rel="next" (preserves all original parameters and adds cursor/id filters). Repeat using each new response's Link header. Stop when the Link header is absent and the array is empty. Expected: further issues, titles at $[].title.
steps.doneWhen: Loop ends when no Link header is returned and the array is empty. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

empty. You should use only the given link to retrieve the next page instead of

fields: NEXT_PAGE_URL: URL from prior response Link header rel="next"
Stop when Link header absent and result empty
